summary.text: A riverine LGA on the Niger and Anambra rivers. Its headquarters, Nzam, is home to indigenous Igala speakers, as are the Olumbanasa communities; the Igbo speaking Anam clan lives here too.

peoples.name: Igala (Nzam and Olumbanasa)
peoples.note: Bilingual in Igala and Igbo. Their share is disputed: the owner says most people in these communities are Igala, while Amali and Bieresnu-Nnabugwu (2023) call them a small group.

languageUse.text: The South East survey finds that the minority language communities of the zone are bilingual, speaking their own language and the nearest Igbo dialect.

livelihoods.text: Fishing, farming (yam, cassava, maize and vegetables) and trade at markets such as Eke Nnokwa and Owelle Central.
